title: AFR 64-4 Survival Manual: Civilian Field Edition: The Air Force's Legendary Survival Train
description: The light is going. The trail you were sure of is gone. Your phone just lost its last bar. Your life probably won't depend on what's in your pack. It will depend on the next few choices you make. For decades, Air Force Regulation 64-4 was the textbook behind U.S. Air Force survival training, known to hunters and hikers as the survival bible. It was brilliant for its time. But it was written for aircrew down in hostile territory, it ran to nearly 600 pages, and some of its old first-aid advice is now known to cause harm. This Civilian Field Edition keeps what still works, cuts the combat material most people will never need, and checks the medical and safety guidance against today's recommendations. The result is a clear, practical manual you can actually use on a dark trail, a snowbound highway, or a cold lake. Every skill follows the same simple field format, so you always know where to look: - When to use it - What you need - The numbered steps - The deadly mistake to avoid - A practical field note Inside you'll learn how to: - Handle the first ten minutes with the S.T.O.P. method and a size-up that puts every threat in the right order - Stop severe bleeding, apply a tourniquet, and recognize and treat shock - Spot hypothermia, frostbite, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke early, and act fast - Respond to snakebites, severe allergic reactions, broken bones, and lightning - Build five shelters before dark, from a ten-minute trash-bag bivy to a snow trench - Start a fire when everything is wet - Find, collect, and treat water you can trust - Get found with a signal mirror, ground-to-air codes, a whistle, and satellite SOS - Navigate with a map and compass, the sun, and the stars when your phone dies - Make the hardest call of all: stay put or walk out - Survive snow count

title: Warrior to Civilian: The Field Manual for the Hero's Journey
description: Winner of the 2026 Axiom Book Awards Gold Medal in Career (Job Search/Career Advancement) A compassionate, practical guidebook for veterans transitioning from active duty to civilian life and for the loved ones supporting their journey. "Challenging yet reassuring....a key addition to every veteran’s packing list ." --Stan McChrystal, General, US Army (Ret) and Co-Founder and CEO, McChrystal Group Some important statistics: There are over 22 million veterans alive today Each year, more than 200,000 new veterans transition out of active duty. Approximately 22 veterans commit suicide a day, and even more are living with PTSD, traumatic brain injury (TBI), struggling with substance abuse, homelessness, and experience many, many other difficulties. It's clear that we have not honored the promise we make to veterans: that we as a country will help them after they've served and sacrificed. And while there are many books written by and for veterans, only a small selection of those address the transition to civilian life, and none are a truly complete reference for stepping out of service and back into normal life. Warrior to Civilian covers a range of topics, from the practical—finding a job, reintegrating into family life—to the more challenging topics, like dealing with loss, and finding new purpose in life. This well-curated resource incorporates stories, insights, and observations from veterans and their partners; evidence-based advice from health professionals and experts who work closely with veterans; and inspiration taken from heavyweights like Jon Kabbat-Zinn and Tony Robbins. The authors take care to address the unique challenges faced by veterans of color, and those in the LGBTQ+ communities. With support from some of our country's most recognizable military members

title: Guidebook For Civilians: The Field Manual for Marines Returning to Unregulated Space
description: You survived recruit training, the field and every inspection the Corps could throw at you. Now you face something worse: civilians. They walk four abreast on the sidewalk. They say “No worries” when there are worries. They hold meetings about meetings, park their grocery carts across the whole aisle, and nobody has called a cadence in years. Guidebook for Civilians is the field manual every Marine should have been issued on the way out the gate. Written in the dead-serious voice of the real thing, one numbered paragraph at a time, it covers everything the separated Marine needs to survive in unregulated space: • The 11 General Orders of a Civilian (“To take charge of this recliner and all snacks in view”) • The Civilian’s Creed (“This is my recliner. There are many like it, but this one is mine.”) • Immediate action drills for the TV remote • Bureaucratic defensive combat at the DMV • Interrogation resistance for Thanksgiving dinner • Grill command, and the passing of the tongs • The Voice Volume Chart, the Checkout Line Selection Matrix, and the Threat Assessment of Relatives • The Civilian Code of Conduct Every chapter ends with a Chapter Review, so you can be sure the knowledge sticks. A perfect gift for any Marine getting out, retiring, or still adjusting thirty years later, and for the families who have to live with them. From L. C. “Tom” Tomlinson Jr., a retired Marine Master Gunnery Sergeant, two-tour Vietnam veteran and former Chief Drill Instructor at MCRD San Diego. He has been a civilian for more than thirty years. title: Urban Preparedness Field Guide: Practical Awareness, Safety, and Confidence for Everyday C
description: Cities have changed. Not in obvious ways, but in subtle shifts that affect how we move through public spaces, commute, travel, and interact with the world around us. Urban Tactical Concepts (UTC) is a practical guide to developing situational awareness, recognizing behavioral patterns, and making smarter decisions in everyday environments. Drawing from research in behavioral psychology, threat assessment, and risk management, this book bridges the gap between what most people know about personal safety and what they need to know to navigate modern urban life with confidence. This is not a survivalist manual, nor is it driven by fear. Instead, it offers a balanced, evidence-based approach to personal security—teaching readers how to stay aware without becoming anxious, prepared without becoming paranoid. title: The Ranger Handbook: Civilian Field Guide 2025 (Annotated)
description: Based on TC 3-21.76, dated 19 September 2025, this annotated civilian edition adds original commentary, context, and guidance for non-military readers. It is not an official Department of Defense publication. Instead of presenting the source material as a bare reproduction, this edition adds structured explanation and recurring editorial guidance so readers can grasp the key ideas, language, and practical lessons without having to decode every acronym, assumption, or doctrinal reference on their own. This annotated edition includes: Explanatory notes clarifying doctrine and terminology Chapter briefs and chapter debriefs Jargon decoding and civilian context Practical commentary and quick-reference learning aids Inside this book, you’ll find: leadership under pressure and command principles mission planning, patrols, and structured decision-making communications, movement, and field discipline battle drills, urban operations, and other military-heavy doctrine sections first aid, trauma response, readiness, and practical field knowledge recurring editorial guidance and quick-reference summaries This book is especially suited for readers interested in: military doctrine explained for civilians leadership that works in real conditions fieldcraft and outdoor competence structured thinking under stress disciplined planning and decision-making Some sections are primarily presented for doctrinal literacy and structured learning rather than direct civilian application. title: First Aid - FM 4-25.11 US Army Field Manual (2002 Civilian Reference Edition): Unabridged
description: Learn to Master First Aid For The Unexpected And For When Help Is Delayed Prepare yourself and brush up on your skills with this unabridged, high-quality Civilian Reference Edition reissue of the official First Aid US Department of The Army Field Manual FM 4-25.11, 2002 release (also published as FM 21-11, NTRP 4-02.1, AFMAN 44-163[I]). This is the latest edition of the US Army First Aid manual. Contents include basic first aid; evaluating injuries and casualties; breathing and airway; bleeding and wound protection; shock; various wounds on specific parts of the body; bandages; fractures and splinting; burns; heat and cold injuries; insects, bites, and stings; nuclear/biological/chemical situations; psychological and mental stress considerations for first aid; first aid kids and equipment; carries, transport, and airlifts; and theories of first aid and rescue. Gain essential backcountry first aid skills for trail, camp, and survival with this unabridged reprint of the official 2002 First Aid manual from the US Army. Or prep up on your first aid skills for self-sustainable living and homesteading to be prepared for anything that comes your way. A part of the Military Outdoors Skills Series: Volume 3 This Doublebit Historic Edition reprint of First Aid, FM 4-25.11 - 2002 is professionally restored and presented from the original source with the highest degree of fidelity possible. Available in both paperback and hardcover, readers can enjoy this Civilian Reference Edition reissue for generations to come and learn from its timeless knowledge. title: Ready, Actually: A Civilian’s Field Guide to Britain’s New Security Age
description: The front line moved, and nobody sent you a memo. For thirty years, we lived on a comfortable assumption: major wars in Europe were history, and "national security" was a job for professionals in uniform. In 2022, the future finally sent the bill. But if you think modern defense is still just about tanks, frigates, and generals, you’re looking at the wrong map. The new front line doesn't just run through trenches. It runs through hospital server rooms, undersea internet cables, high-street payment systems, and your neighborhood group chats. Ready, Actually is a civilian’s field guide to Britain’s new security age. It is emphatically not a doomsday survival manual. It won’t tell you to buy a generator, stockpile canned beans, or be afraid. Fear is fast, fear is stupid, and fear is exactly what an adversary wants from you. Written—with a heavy dose of irony—by a Russian-born tech founder and pacifist living in London, this book points out what the natives have stopped noticing. Britain has a massive, untapped arsenal of everyday resilience hiding in plain sight. You’ll discover: The Porcupine Principle: Why the goal isn't to be a chest-beating lion, but a porcupine—so calmly, boringly difficult to attack that nobody sensible even tries. The Four Layers of Reality: Why the military "shield" is only a fraction of the story, and why the real targets are your nervous system, bloodstream, and social fabric. The Hollywood Filter: Why Britain's recruitment crisis is actually a "meaning" problem, and why the military is only a tiny sliver of how a citizen can serve. The Tech Reality Check: Why engineers who flinch at the word "defence" are exactly the people who need to be building it. title: The Civilian Counter-Surveillance Field Manual: Detection Gear, Secure Data, Field Testing
description: The Civilian Counter-Surveillance Field Manual Detection Gear, Secure Data, Field Testing, and Lawful Privacy Protection Privacy gear is easy to buy. Knowing what it can actually tell you is harder. The Civilian Counter-Surveillance Field Manual is a practical guide to building and testing a lawful civilian privacy toolkit without turning every blinking light into a conspiracy theory. It shows you how to choose equipment by the question you need answered, test it under real conditions, understand its blind spots, protect the files it creates, and stay inside ethical and legal boundaries. Written for travelers, property managers, consultants, security-minded professionals, small business owners, and anyone who wants a calmer, more disciplined approach to privacy protection, this book replaces gadget hype with repeatable field methods. Inside, you will learn how to: - Build a civilian privacy toolkit around decisions instead of shopping lists. - Run visual, optical, network, and passive RF privacy checks in spaces you are authorized to inspect. - Understand what consumer hidden-camera and signal detectors can and cannot prove. - Choose cameras, microphones, wearables, and field computers by distance, light, noise, battery life, and workflow. - Test gear with known-present and known-absent checks before relying on it. - Separate useful evidence from false positives and unexplained readings. - Create power plans that survive real shifts instead of brochure conditions. - Preserve originals, encrypt sensitive material, manage access, and build clean data handoffs. - Evaluate emerging AI-assisted detection products without mistaking confidence scores for facts. - Maintain batteries, storage media, firmware, cables, and accessories before small failures become expensive ones. -

title: After the Uniform: A Field Manual for Civilian Life
description: The mission isn’t over—it just changed uniforms. Whether you're days away from ETS, counting down to retirement, or years into your Guard/Reserve journey, After the Uniform is your practical guide to navigating the civilian world without losing your identity, purpose, or sanity. This book will teach you how to: Translate your military experience into a civilian resume and job interview that lands offers Rebuild a sense of purpose without rank or uniform Navigate family dynamics and reintegration after service Take charge of your mental, physical, and financial health Reconnect with community and rebuild your support network Let go of control and lead with influence in the civilian world If you’ve ever thought: “Who am I without the uniform?” “Why doesn’t civilian work make sense?” “How do I find purpose again?” This is your field manual. Real stories. Real strategies. No fluff. title: AFR 64-4 Survival Handbook (Annotated): The Essential Illustrated Civilian Guide to Surviv
description: Prepare for your next outdoor trip with clear explanations and a place to start. Have you opened a survival manual and struggled to turn its instructions into something you can actually practice? When daylight is fading or the weather changes, can you explain your next decision? Would you like a clear way to prepare your equipment, plan an outing, and build useful skills a little at a time? A military manual can contain valuable lessons while assuming equipment, training, and circumstances a civilian reader does not share. Isolated tips leave you to work out the priorities, the limits, and whether a practice attempt went well. Start with an explanation. Follow a practical task. Check the result. AFR 64-4 Survival Handbook (Annotated) is an abridged and illustrated civilian study edition built around the 1985 manual's 31 chapters. Original commentary, selected historical excerpts, and references to contemporary guidance help you understand the ideas and apply them to outdoor preparation. It is not a reproduction of the complete original text. Build a plan you can use and skills you can practice. Understand the priorities . Work through stress, changing conditions, and practical decisions before a small problem grows. Prepare for exposure . Study clothing, shelter, fire, food, and water with civilian examples and explanations of important limits. Plan your movement and communication . Learn map-reading tasks, route decisions, trip planning, signaling, and useful information to give rescuers. See what the text means . Black-and-white illustrations and distinct commentary notes help you follow the explanation and return to key points. Test your understanding .
